general_skills.title: Decompose Before Searching
general_skills.principle: Break complex questions into minimal facts and retrieve each fact separately before synthesizing the answer.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Questions involving multiple entities, relations, comparisons, or dependent facts.

general_skills.title: Use Entity Plus Attribute Queries
general_skills.principle: Construct concise queries from the exact entity name and the missing attribute instead of repeating the full question.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Every initial fact lookup and any follow-up lookup for a known entity.

general_skills.title: Refine Rather Than Repeat
general_skills.principle: When evidence is weak, reformulate with aliases, dates, roles, locations, or quoted phrases; never submit the unchanged query repeatedly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: The retrieved passages are empty, ambiguous, or do not explicitly contain the requested fact.

general_skills.title: Resolve Entity Ambiguity
general_skills.principle: Disambiguate shared names by adding occupation, nationality, work title, year, or another relation from the question.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Search results mix multiple people, works, organizations, or places with the same name.

general_skills.title: Answer Only From Evidence
general_skills.principle: Do not finalize until a retrieved passage directly supports the answer; treat unsupported model memory as a hypothesis to verify.

general_skills.title: Preserve Exact Answer Form
general_skills.principle: Return only the requested name, date, number, place, or short phrase and preserve distinctions that matter for exact-match scoring.

general_skills.title: Stop When Evidence Is Sufficient
general_skills.principle: Once reliable evidence directly answers the question, stop searching and provide the answer instead of accumulating redundant passages.
general_skills.when_to_apply: A passage explicitly states the requested fact and no unresolved comparison remains.

general_skills.title: Track Retrieved Facts
general_skills.principle: Maintain a compact list of established entities and attributes so later queries build on evidence instead of restarting the reasoning chain.

direct_retrieval.title: Core Fact Query
direct_retrieval.principle: Search the subject together with the requested fact, such as author, release date, birthplace, population, or winner.
direct_retrieval.when_to_apply: Single-hop who, what, when, or where questions.

direct_retrieval.title: Quote Distinctive Titles
direct_retrieval.principle: Put distinctive song, book, film, episode, or quoted phrases in quotation marks and append the requested attribute.
direct_retrieval.when_to_apply: The question contains a named creative work or exact phrase.

direct_retrieval.title: Use Answer-Type Constraints
direct_retrieval.principle: Add a type cue such as actor, city, year, number of episodes, or organization when generic results dominate.
direct_retrieval.when_to_apply: The first query retrieves the right topic but not the requested answer type.

direct_retrieval.title: Extract Minimal Span
direct_retrieval.principle: Read the passage for the exact answer span and return the shortest unambiguous form.
direct_retrieval.when_to_apply: The relevant passage contains a longer sentence around a short factoid answer.

entity_attribute_lookup.title: Entity Attribute Pair
entity_attribute_lookup.principle: Search the canonical entity name followed by the requested property, avoiding unrelated context from the original question.
entity_attribute_lookup.when_to_apply: PopQA-style occupation, birthplace, genre, nationality, or affiliation questions.

entity_attribute_lookup.title: Find Canonical Entity Name
entity_attribute_lookup.principle: If the entity is an alias or partial name, first retrieve its canonical name, then query the desired property.
entity_attribute_lookup.when_to_apply: Initial results do not clearly identify the intended entity.

entity_attribute_lookup.title: Prefer Biographical Statements
entity_attribute_lookup.principle: Look for passages that explicitly use patterns such as 'is a', 'was born in', 'member of', or 'known for'.
entity_attribute_lookup.when_to_apply: The requested attribute is biographical or categorical.

entity_attribute_lookup.title: Reject Neighbor Attributes
entity_attribute_lookup.principle: Verify that the passage describes the queried entity rather than a related person, parent organization, work, or location.
entity_attribute_lookup.when_to_apply: A passage contains several entities and several candidate attributes.

multi_hop_reasoning.title: Identify the Bridge Entity
multi_hop_reasoning.principle: Determine which intermediate person, work, place, or organization connects the subject of the question to the requested answer.
multi_hop_reasoning.when_to_apply: The answer is an attribute of an entity that is not directly named.

multi_hop_reasoning.title: One Hop Per Query
multi_hop_reasoning.principle: Retrieve the first relation, record the intermediate entity, then issue a second query for that entity's requested attribute.
multi_hop_reasoning.when_to_apply: Two or more facts must be chained.

multi_hop_reasoning.title: Verify Every Link
multi_hop_reasoning.principle: Require explicit evidence for both the source-to-bridge relation and the bridge-to-answer relation.

multi_hop_reasoning.title: Use Intermediate Names Verbatim
multi_hop_reasoning.principle: Copy the canonical intermediate entity name from the retrieved passage into the next search query.
multi_hop_reasoning.when_to_apply: Moving from one hop to the next.

compare.title: Retrieve Values Independently
compare.principle: Search for each entity's relevant value separately instead of asking the search engine to perform the comparison.
compare.when_to_apply: Questions asking earlier, later, larger, smaller, older, younger, or whether attributes match.

compare.title: Normalize Comparable Values
compare.principle: Convert retrieved facts to the same representation, such as four-digit years, full dates, or numeric counts, before comparing.
compare.when_to_apply: The two passages express values in different formats.

compare.title: Keep Entity-Value Bindings
compare.principle: Record each value beside its entity so the final comparison cannot swap which fact belongs to which subject.
compare.when_to_apply: After each side of a comparison is retrieved.

compare.title: Return the Requested Comparison Form
compare.principle: If the question asks which entity satisfies the comparison, answer with that entity rather than only returning the compared value.
compare.when_to_apply: The final reasoning step of a comparison question.

common_mistakes.description: Repeating the full natural-language question as every search query.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent does not isolate the missing fact.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Use concise entity-plus-attribute queries and reformulate after weak results.

common_mistakes.description: Answering from model memory before retrieving supporting evidence.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: A familiar-looking entity creates false confidence.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Verify the exact fact in a retrieved passage before answering.

common_mistakes.description: Emitting search and answer tags in the same action.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent mixes tool use with termination.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Choose exactly one action per turn.

common_mistakes.description: Skipping an intermediate relation in a multi-hop question.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent jumps from the named subject to a plausible answer.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Write down and verify the bridge entity before the final lookup.

common_mistakes.description: Returning an explanatory sentence that obscures the exact-match answer.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent optimizes for prose rather than factoid evaluation.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Place only the shortest unambiguous answer inside the answer tags.
